title: A01:2021 Broken Access Control
text: A01:2021 Broken Access Control. Access control enforces policy so users cannot act outside their intended permissions. Failures include acting as another user, viewing or modifying another account's data, and missing server-side checks on network-exposed endpoints. In NDR telemetry look for a single identity or host touching many object identifiers, unusual HTTP 403/401 clusters followed by 200 responses, or direct object-reference enumeration. Respond by confirming the identity, revoking the session, and fixing the missing authorization check.

title: A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures
text: A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures. Cryptographic failures cover data exposed because encryption is missing, weak, or misused: plaintext protocols, weak TLS versions or ciphers, hard-coded keys, and missing certificate validation. Network detection: TLS 1.0/1.1 or null-cipher negotiation, plaintext HTTP/FTP/Telnet to sensitive services, self-signed or expired certificates in unexpected places. Response is to terminate the weak path, rotate exposed secrets, and enforce a modern TLS policy.

title: A03:2021 Injection
text: A03:2021 Injection. Injection occurs when untrusted data reaches an interpreter: SQL, NoSQL, OS command, ORM, LDAP, or XSS in the browser. Network signatures include SQL metacharacters in request parameters, union/select patterns, time-based blind probes, and script tags in reflected parameters. Respond by blocking the source at the edge, preserving the request as evidence, and fixing parameterised queries or output encoding.

title: A04:2021 Insecure Design
text: A04:2021 Insecure Design. Insecure design is a missing or ineffective control at the design level, not an implementation bug. Threat modelling, secure design patterns and reference architectures are required. In operations this appears as business flows that can be abused at scale, such as unlimited password reset or unrestricted scraping. Response is a design change with layered controls, not a single edge rule.

title: A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration
text: A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration. The most common category: default accounts and passwords, unnecessary features or ports, verbose errors, missing hardening, permissive CORS, and missing security headers. Network detection: management planes exposed to user networks, default service banners, directory listing, and unusual outbound services. Response is to close the exposure, remove defaults, and add configuration baselines with drift detection.

title: A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components
text: A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components. Components with known vulnerabilities or unsupported versions. Detection is indirect at the network layer: exploit attempts against a known CVE, version disclosure in banners, or a host requesting updates over cleartext. Response is to identify the exact component and version, patch or isolate, and verify no successful exploitation occurred before patching.

title: A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures
text: A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures. Weak authentication permits credential stuffing, brute force, default credentials, and session fixation. Network signals: many authentication failures across few accounts, one source spraying many accounts, impossible-travel logins, and session tokens reused from different networks. Respond by throttling or blocking the source, locking targeted identities, enforcing MFA, and checking for a successful login after the failures.

title: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
text: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures. Code and data are accepted without integrity verification: unsigned updates, insecure deserialization, and CI/CD pipeline compromise. Network signals: hosts fetching updates over HTTP, unexpected package registries, and serialized object payloads to application endpoints. Respond by stopping the update path, verifying signatures, and rebuilding from a trusted artifact.

title: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
text: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures. Detection requires sufficient logging, retention, and alerting. Failures include missing audit events, logs that are not monitored, and alerts with no response path. NDR relevance: if flow or authentication telemetry is missing for an asset, an attack against it is invisible. Response is to restore sensor coverage, define retention, and test the detection-to-response path.

title: A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery
text: A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery. SSRF occurs when a server fetches a URL supplied by the user, allowing access to internal services or cloud metadata. Network signals: an application host making requests to internal RFC1918 ranges, link-local metadata addresses, or unusual external destinations. Respond by blocking the egress path at the application boundary, restricting allowed destinations, and reviewing what the request reached.
